chunks: A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ja'far ibn Muhammad al-Ash'ari, from Ibn al-Qaddah, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

Rasool-Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Jibraeel (peace be upon him) did not cease to advise me with the siwak (brushing of the teeth) to the extent that I feared being toothless and with thin teeth'.
ai.seo_question: Why did the Prophet fear losing his teeth according to the hadith about siwak?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi highlights the high status of siwak in Shia tradition, linking it directly to the continuous revelation of divine instruction via Jibraeel. The phrase 'khishitu an adrad wa uhfiya' (I feared my teeth would fall out or become thin) is interpreted by scholars as either a literal concern or a rhetorical expression of the practice's importance, emphasizing its role in purifying the mouth for prayer and recitation. It underscores the Prophetic emphasis on physical cleanliness as an integral component of spiritual discipline.

en.hubeali:
A number of our companions, from Sahl Bin Ziyad, from Ja’far Bin Muhammad Al Ashary, from Ibn Al Qaddah, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:

‘Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> said: ‘Jibraeel<sup>as</sup> did not cease to advise me<sup>saww</sup> with brushing of the teeth to the extent that I<sup>saww</sup> feared being toothless and with thin teeth’.
en.sarwar: 3. A number of our people have narrated from Sahl ibn Ziyad from Ja‘far ibn Muhammad al-Ash‘ariy from ibn al-Qaddah who has said the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said that the Messenger of Allah, O Allah, grant compensation to Muhammad and his family worthy of their services to Your cause, has said, ‘
Jibril continued urging me to brush so much so that I feared of becoming toothless or wearing them thin.’”
